invd.H: 87 → 100 days: ~33 of cash tied up vs 2022 level

dpo.H: Not used as a lever: stretching suppliers during a downgrade is high-risk

br_gp.H: OEM pricing, input & energy costs, mix — the COO and Auto sales head are both right

br_ben.A: Digital gross benefits realised in COGS (2025)

br_chk.A: Check: bridge end − reported 2025 EBITDA (should be 0)

br_seg_auto.H: Auto explains ~2/3 of the Group decline

sc_netrr.H: PdM and Vision pay their running costs; SCP does not

sc_tgt.H: PdM 60%, Vision 48%; SCP negative — inventory days rose 90 → 94

sc_payback.A: Years of net recurring benefit to recover capitalised spend
sc_payback.H: At current scope, even the winners take 18–25 years: scale and adoption are the issue, not the technology

dig_chk.A: Check: vs Ex.1 digital opex (should be 0)

dig_net.A: Net digital P&L 2025 (benefits − all digital opex)
dig_net.H: Digital is currently a −35 drag on a 25 EBITDA business

rem26.A: Remaining implementation work required in 2026 (current scope)

rolloff.H: Temporary costs do not recur (Ex.6). Base case gets this too — our plan must beat it

au_proj.A: Pilot project opex borne by Auto
au_proj.H: Pilots sit in 2 Auto plants of 3 per project → 2/3 share (assumption)

au_cent.A: Central digital cost allocated to Auto (by revenue)

au_net.A: Net digital drag on Auto EBITDA

au_ex.A: Auto EBITDA excluding net digital drag

au_exm.A: Auto EBITDA margin excluding net digital drag
au_exm.H: Still far below 11.1% in 2022 → the rest is pricing/volume/input cost: digital must reach commercial & procurement

vis_cov.A: Implied covered-line production cost (benefit ÷ scrap-point reduction)

vis_share.A: Implied share of Group cost of sales on 8 lines
vis_share.H: Implausible for 8 lines → benefit likely includes inspection-labour savings. We do NOT extrapolate this ratio; new lines are haircut 50%

a_real.D: Pilots achieved 48–60% of targeted KPI gains (Ex.7); benchmark levers are already sized well below published ranges → 75% sits between. 100% = stretch, 50% = downside (Sensitivity). Not applied to F3 (contractual cost removal)

a_auto.A: Auto share of pilot project cost & benefit
a_auto.D: Each pilot runs in 2 Auto plants out of 3 (Ex.7); allocation by plant count

a_costf.A: Incremental recurring cost per unit when scaling, vs pilot per-unit cost
a_costf.D: Platform licences, monitoring and team are shared, so scaling costs less than the pilot per unit

a_rate.A: Interest rate on debt (before refinancing premium)
a_rate.D: 2025 implied: 40 ÷ average debt of 742 (Diagnosis). Applied to opening debt each period (avoids circularity)

a_prem.A: Refinancing premium on rolled-over short-term debt and all new money
a_prem.D: Assumption: +300bp for a borrower on downgrade watch; applied from Jan-26 to the 180 of short-term debt and to every dollar of new borrowing

a_mincash.D: Held at the 2025 closing level; any shortfall is funded by debt

a_tax.D: PBT stays negative through Jun-27 in every case (checked on Projection); no cash tax

a_da.A: D&A per year (for PBT check only)
a_da.D: Held at 2025 level; used only to confirm PBT < 0

a_capss.A: Steady-state digital capex per year after the mandate
a_capss.D: Used only for the run-rate cash break-even test

a_revflat.A: Revenue and underlying gross margin held at 2025 levels
a_revflat.D: No market recovery and no further erosion assumed. OEM price-down and volume risks shown on Sensitivity

b_exp.A: Base: upgrade & expansion capex per year

b_split.A: Base: share of 18-month digital capex spent in 2026

p_maint.A: Maintenance capex per year (plan and base)
p_maint.D: NOT reduced: already below PPE depreciation of 50 (Ex.4); case requires justification for any cut

p_exp.A: Plan: upgrade & expansion capex per year
p_exp.D: Defer expansion: utilisation is 72% Auto, 81% IEM, 67% SMC (Ex.8), so no business is capacity-constrained. Keep 10 for safety/debottlenecking

f1_capex.A: F1 Master data & ERP harmonisation: capex
f1_capex.D: Redirect the SCP capex request (10) to move the 3 local-system plants onto the shared ERP in waves + master-data tooling

f1_oneoff.D: Uses the SCP remaining-work budget (3.0), repurposed to data cleansing and governance

f1_rec.A: F1: recurring cost (data stewards, MDM tool)
f1_rec.D: Assumption: ~5 data stewards across plants + MDM licence

f2_rec.A: F2 Digital Value Office: recurring cost
f2_rec.D: Chief Digital Officer reporting to CEO + 4 business product owners + value tracking; central team of 24 reallocated, not added

f3_lic.D: Keep the core planning tool so planners keep working and data fixes can be tested

f3_cloud.D: Smaller footprint once agent layer is off

f3_tok.D: Switch off the agentic layer: 35% acceptance, inventory days worse (Ex.7)

f3_trans.D: Case requires an explicit assumption (Ex.6). 2026 commitments (2.0) are below the retained run-cost (3.1) and lapse without penalty from Jan-27

s1_tgt.A: S1 PdM current cohort: target downtime by Jun-27
s1_tgt.D: 12% → 7.5% = 37.5% reduction, inside McKinsey's 30–50% range [B1]; short of the 7% business-case target given technician constraints

s1_rec.A: S1: recurring cost (technician capacity, work-order integration upkeep)
s1_rec.D: Close the loop: alerts closed in window 60% → 85% (month-6 gate)

s2_assets.A: S2 PdM scale-up: additional connected assets
s2_assets.D: Doubles the cohort, IEM-led (81% utilisation, growing); released only after the S1 gate

s2_real.A: S2: benefit per asset vs pilot
s2_real.D: Haircut for new plants and lower data readiness (40% machine-data coverage, Ex.8)

s2_auto.A: S2: share of new assets in Auto

s2_oneoff.D: Integration + model tuning for new assets

s2_capex.D: Approve the PdM request (Ex.5), released in tranches after the gate

s3_tgt.A: S3 Vision current lines: target scrap/rework by Jun-27
s3_tgt.D: 6.0% → 4.2% = 72% of targeted improvement (vs 48% today) via retraining and a calibration workflow for spec changes

s3_oneoff.D: Remaining 2026 work (2.0) is already in the base case

s4_lines.A: S4 Vision + traceability: additional Auto lines (gated, one named OEM programme)
s4_lines.D: Only where an OEM programme demands part-level traceability; capex released after month-9 gate. EBITDA-neutral — justified as customer retention, so kept small

s4_hair.A: S4: benefit per line vs pilot average
s4_hair.D: Pilot ratio implies implausible covered cost (Diagnosis §8) → 50% haircut

s4_oneoff.D: Stations, calibration for new part families

s4_capex.D: Cut the 12 request to 4: three Auto lines for one OEM programme

n1_auto.A: N1 Energy management: saving on Auto energy (forging)
n1_auto.D: Sub-metering + load scheduling + furnace optimisation. ISO 50001 plants ~4.1% in year 1 [B3]; APC up to 10% energy reduction [B2]

n1_smc.D: Batch heating/curing: energy is 23% of SMC revenue (Ex.8)

n1_capex.D: Needed: only 40% of equipment has central machine data (Ex.8)

n2_yield.A: N2 SMC golden-batch / process control: yield gain on SMC materials & other cost
n2_yield.D: APC delivers up to 5% yield [B2]. Sized on materials only (energy excluded) → no overlap with N1. Funded only if SMC passes the month-6 gate

n3_addr.A: N3 Procurement analytics: addressable share of non-energy, non-labour COGS
n3_addr.D: COGS 930 − energy 120 − labour 180 = 630; ~70% is bought-in materials & parts (assumption)

n3_sav.A: N3: net saving on addressable spend
n3_sav.D: Far below the 6–12% McKinsey observes in chemicals procurement [B4]

n4_auto.A: N4 Commercial: index-linked cost pass-through, Auto
n4_auto.D: NOT a list-price rise: inserts energy/raw-material index clauses at named OEM contract renewals, recovering inflation Ironbridge absorbed. Pricing programmes add 2–7pp ROS [B5]

n4_iem.D: Configuration flexibility is valued (Ex.8); CPQ cuts quote lead time and discount leakage

n4_smc.A: N4: price realisation, SMC (cost pass-through, specialty value pricing)
n4_smc.D: SMC EBITDA fell 15 in 2025 on flat revenue → energy/input inflation not passed on. Specialty coatings carry more pricing power than auto parts

n4_rec.A: N4: recurring cost (pricing analysts, CPQ licence)

n5_rev.A: N5 IEM connected-service pilot: service revenue as % of IEM revenue by Jun-27
n5_rev.D: Remote monitoring + predictive service on installed pumps/drives, reusing the PdM stack

n5_margin.A: N5: EBITDA margin on service revenue
n5_margin.D: Aftermarket services average 25% EBIT vs 10% for new equipment [B6]; haircut for start-up

n5_capex.A: N5: capex (sensor kits for pilot fleet)

n6_base.A: N6 Back-office & customer-support automation: addressable cost
n6_base.D: Non-digital personnel (108) + selling & customer support (45): up 28 since 2022 while revenue rose 3.5% (Ex.1)

n6_sav.A: N6: productivity saving on addressable cost
n6_sav.D: GenAI in customer care: 30–45% of function cost [B8]; automation of the 3 plants' manual month-end consolidation (Ex.8). Delivered via attrition and hiring freeze

n6_rec.A: N6: recurring cost (GenAI licences, tokens, automation upkeep)
n6_rec.D: Token spend budgeted explicitly — the SCP lesson (Ex.6)

o_claw.A: O2: share of Auto procurement savings passed back to OEMs
o_claw.D: Index-linked clauses work both ways: cheaper indexed materials flow through to OEM prices. Applied to Auto's revenue share of N3

o_give.A: O3: share of Auto productivity savings conceded in OEM annual price-downs
o_give.D: Auto OEMs typically ask for annual productivity give-backs; applied to Auto's share of PdM, vision and energy savings

w_inv26.D: From 100. 2026: slow-mover clean-up and safety-stock reset only (does not need the planning tool)

w_inv27.D: After F1 master data: 2023 level was 88. A 10% cut vs 30% achieved in a McKinsey SC case [B7]

w_dso26.D: From 52.8. E-invoicing, collections analytics, dispute resolution

fs_disp.D: Precedent in the case: non-core licences sold at carrying value — 19 (2024), 31 (2025); 113 of other intangibles remain (Ex.2, Ex.4)

fs_slb.D: Assumption: ~6% of 680 net PPE. Creates a lease liability: buys liquidity, not deleveraging

fs_scf.D: Assumption: ~15% of 172 receivables, on OEM-backed programmes

sh_cm.D: Assumption: materials, energy and ~half of direct labour vary with volume

t_liq.A: Liquidity: new money needed beyond rolling the 180 and identified sources — at most
t_liq.D: The company can fund the mandate without asking lenders for fresh money (2025: FCF −141)

t_cov.A: Solvency: exit run-rate interest cover in the DOWNSIDE case (50% realisation) — at least

t_auto_pl.A: Auto plants' share of maintenance capex (5 of 11 plants)

eb.H: Momentum run-rate + benefits × factor − recurring costs

lev.A: Net debt / run-rate EBITDA (net debt at base-case plan)

f15.A: Realisation needed for run-rate interest cover of 1.5x

f20.A: Realisation needed for run-rate interest cover of 2.0x

sh_vol.H: At 25% contribution margin; utilisation would fall further below 72%

sh_energy.H: Energy is 120 of COGS; N1 metering and N4 index clauses partly hedge

sh_comm.A: Procurement & pass-through deliver only this share

sh_rate.H: Interest, not EBITDA: applied to the 180 + new money

src_B1.B: Predictive maintenance typically reduces machine downtime by 30–50% and increases machine life by 20–40%
src_B1.C: McKinsey & Company, "Manufacturing: Analytics unleashes productivity and profitability", 14 Aug 2017

src_B2.B: Optimised advanced process controls: up to 15% more throughput, 5% more yield, 10% less energy
src_B2.C: McKinsey & Company, "The potential of advanced process controls in energy and materials", 23 Nov 2020

src_B3.B: ISO 50001-certified facilities achieve ~4.1% annual energy-performance improvement in the first year and ~3.4% after twelve years
src_B3.C: Fitzgerald, Therkelsen, Sheaffer, Rao (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory), "Deeper and persistent energy savings and CO2 reductions achieved through ISO 50001 in the manufacturing sector", 2023

src_B4.B: Reducing overall spending by 6–12% is a realistic goal in chemicals procurement
src_B4.C: McKinsey & Company, "Technology-enabled procurement for chemical companies", 1 Oct 2019

src_B5.B: Across 1,000+ pricing-excellence initiatives, return on sales typically rises 2–7 percentage points
src_B5.C: McKinsey & Company, "Turning pricing power into profit", 1 Mar 2015

src_B6.B: Average EBIT margin for aftermarket services 25% vs 10% for new equipment (30 industries)
src_B6.C: McKinsey & Company, "Industrial aftermarket services: Growing the core", 27 Jul 2017

src_B7.B: Diagnosed ~20% inventory-reduction opportunity; achieved 30% reduction with OTIF rising to 95%
src_B7.C: McKinsey & Company, "Supply Chain 4.0: Opportunities to use your supply chain for differentiation", 24 May 2019

src_B8.B: Generative AI applied to customer care could increase productivity by 30–45% of current function costs
src_B8.C: McKinsey & Company, "The economic potential of generative AI: The next productivity frontier", 14 Jun 2023
